messages:
nora: Quick idea: instead of adding more verbose routing headers, what if SDKs emitted a compact base64-encoded route-context token in a single header `X-RW-RouteCtx`? Contains route id + small attrs (priority/env). Would reduce header proliferation. Thoughts?

bryce: I like single header surface, but base64 blobs make console debugging harder. We need ingestion to decode and index key fields (route_id, priority, sdk). Also watch cardinality.

anya: Agreed on decode at ingest. Also: some proxies strip headers with non-alphanumeric content; base64 is usually safe, but some CDNs might block long headers. We should limit encoded size to ~256 bytes and provide truncation rules.

console: Console can decode and index route_id + priority + src_sdk_version. We'll add a small decoded preview in the request flyout and a sparkline showing adoption. But we need stable token schema (v1) and a version byte to handle future expansion.

nora: Proposal: token schema: `v|route_id|priority|sdk:ver` then base64. Example: `v1|route-42|h|py:1.3.2` -> base64. SDKs default to old headers until opt-in env var `RW_ROUTECTX_MODE=dual` then dual-emit for one minor.

bryce: For quota attribution: keep existing `X-Redwood-Route` as primary key. If `X-RW-RouteCtx` present decode it and use route_id for attribution. If both present and mismatch, prefer `X-RW-RouteCtx` and emit alert metric `route.mismatch` sampled.

anya: SDK plan: py/ts/go add helper to build token. Minimal pseudo for py:```python
# build_route_ctx.py
def build_route_ctx(route_id, priority, sdk_ver):
    raw = f"v1|{route_id}|{priority}|{sdk_ver}"
    token = base64.b64encode(raw.encode()).decode()
    if len(token) > 256:
        metrics.increment('route.ctx.truncated')
        token = token[:256]
    return token
headers['X-RW-RouteCtx'] = token
```

bryce: Unit tests: assert decode roundtrip, assert truncation metric fires. In TS ensure Buffer/atob handling for browser vs node.

console: Ingest change: decode token, populate `route_ctx_v` (v1), `route_id`, `route_priority`, `sdk_name`, `sdk_version`. Also add `route_ctx_raw` length and set `route_ctx_source` old/new/both. Backfill historical as `old`.

devops-bot: edge-proxy/shim v6 scheduled -> staging 2026-03-26T09:30:00Z

anya: Ops note: some legacy WAFs block headers with `=` (base64 padding). Recommend urlsafe base64 (replace +/ with -_) and strip padding `=`. That reduces chance of stripping. Update token builder accordingly.

nora: Good call. Use urlsafe base64 without padding. Update pseudo code accordingly.

bryce: Telemetry: emit `route.ctx.seen` sampled 0.2% with labels `sdk`, `sdk_version`, `route_ctx_v`. Also emit `route.ctx.invalid` when decode fails. Console will show a small error percentage.

console: Dashboard UX: add adoption tile and a debug panel that shows decoded token for a sampled set of requests. Also a filter to show all requests where `route_ctx_v != v1` or decode fails.

anya: Rollout steps: 1) SDKs add token builder & env `RW_ROUTECTX_MODE` (off/dual/new-only-canary/new-only). Default off. 2) Minor SDK release (dual opt-in) in 7 days. 3) Shim to map new header -> existing `X-Redwood-Route` for 45 days in case CDNs strip unknown headers (extract route_id and write old header). 4) Console ingest changes and tile in 10 days. 5) Evaluate adoption at 5 weeks; if >85% stable, flip default to dual for one cycle then new-only after 2 weeks.

bryce: Edge-case: if `route_ctx` decodes but route_id is empty, treat as `none` and fallback to old header. Log `route.ctx.empty` sampled 1%.

devops-bot: canary deploy succeeded: edge-proxy/shim v6 -> canary 2026-03-26T09:32:45Z

nora: Docs: include token builder snippet, decoding example, env var semantics, size limits, and troubleshooting tips for customers behind strict proxies. I'll draft the migration guide and a short support FAQ.

sdk-ci: PRs opened: sdk-python#501 (route-ctx), sdk-ts#422, sdk-go#107. CI status: tests pending.

anya: Final ask: add a small per-tenant opt-out flag for shim mapping in case a customer wants to keep using legacy-only keys. Ops will expose that in the tenant console.

nora: Ack. Thanks everyone 680. Closing thread — follow PRs for details.
